candidates.title: Draft logistics event notices

demandEvidence.chore: Draft a dispatcher notice for a shipment delay from a supplied event row.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: A simple flow can notify a dispatcher when a shipment is delayed, copy an order update into a CRM, alert a buyer when inventory drops, or send a daily report to a team channel.

ease.reason: A beginner can map synthetic event rows to a draft notice; no supplied reference supports a live logistics integration.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small logistics operators may pay to reduce delayed shipment updates; this single example establishes no buying intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week text-only mock can accept a supplied delay row and draft a notice; event detection and CRM access remain outside scope.

autonomy.reason: Fixed fields can produce repeatable drafts, but an operator must supply and verify each event and approve any notice.

evidence.reason: The fresh native task span gives concrete logistics notification examples, but only as one article example without frequency or corroboration.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable dispatcher notice draft from one operator-supplied shipment-delay row.
inputs: Synthetic shipment ID, status, expected date, and recipient role.
Operator-supplied event row with a delay flag.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits one sample row for review.
steps: Check that required fields are present.
Apply a fixed rule to identify a delay flag.
Draft a short notice using only supplied fields.
Show missing fields and the source row beside the draft.
Ask an operator to approve or discard it.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a synthetic delayed row, the draft must repeat its shipment ID and date exactly and must not invent missing values.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies and verifies the event row, confirms recipient and business context, and approves any message; no live shipment system or CRM is connected.
unverified: Whether operators repeat this task often enough to buy a service.
Whether real event rows have stable fields.
Whether a safe notification destination and permission can be provided.

candidates.reason: Concrete event-notice example assessed with a bounded mock. The mean is below six; the retained post frames it as an example and supplies no recurrence or buyer validation.

candidates.title: Draft an app review follow-up

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare a concise follow-up asking for an estimated app-review timeline or missing materials.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Could you please share an estimated timeline, or let us know if anything is needed from our side?

ease.reason: A beginner can draft a follow-up from operator-supplied dates and status; no reference supports portal access or response prediction.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: app developers might pay for review tracking, but this is one unresolved case and does not establish a market.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can track submitted date, status and next follow-up date; reviewer response time cannot be predicted.

autonomy.reason: A draft and reminder can be generated from supplied fields, while a person must verify status and send any message.

evidence.reason: The fresh native span states a submission awaiting updates and asks for timeline or required items, but offers no recurrence or corroboration.

experimentPlan.output: A dated, reviewable follow-up draft based on an app submission status record.
inputs: Operator-entered current status and last update date.
experimentPlan.trigger: A person records that an app review remains without an update by the chosen follow-up date.
steps: Check the supplied dates and status for blanks.
Summarize only the recorded submission and update facts.
Draft a neutral request for a timeline or missing materials.
Display the input fields beside the draft.
Ask the operator to verify and send or discard it.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Given a fictional submission record, the draft must preserve its dates and status and must not claim a cause or likely decision.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person enters and verifies the status, chooses when to follow up, and sends the message; the proposal has no review-portal access or reviewer data.
unverified: Whether this is a recurring task for a paying customer group.
Whether manually supplied status remains current.
Whether a neutral reminder draft improves on a calendar reminder.

candidates.reason: The full retained span supports a follow-up chore, but it is a single case; provisional mean is below six and utility beyond a manual reminder is uncertain.

candidates.title: Prepare weekly keyword research rows

demandEvidence.chore: Collect weekly keyword search volume, CPC and difficulty values into rows for a spreadsheet.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: adds each keyword’s Google search volume, CPC and difficulty as rows in Google Sheets.

ease.reason: The post describes a weekly spreadsheet workflow, but no implementation reference is attached and external search data is not verified here.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent marketing consultants may pay to prepare keyword research; this showcase does not establish buyer intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can validate supplied keyword metrics and format rows; obtaining accurate current metrics and writing to Sheets remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A repeatable row-formatting step is plausible, while a person must source, verify and upload the metrics.

evidence.reason: The native span describes a weekly task and named fields, but as one shared-flow example with no independent demand corroboration.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable spreadsheet-ready table of supplied keyword metrics.
inputs: Operator-supplied search volume, CPC and difficulty values.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator provides the weekly keyword list and its sourced metrics.
steps: Check that each row has a keyword and three metric fields.
Format the supplied values into consistent rows.
Show a preview and row-level validation notes.
Ask an operator to verify and copy the rows into a sheet.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: A fixed synthetic input should produce the same number of rows, preserve each value exactly, and flag missing fields without filling them.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person obtains and verifies metrics and copies approved rows; no search provider or spreadsheet connection is proposed as working.
unverified: Whether a specific professional customer repeatedly needs this task.
Whether supplied metrics are accurate and comparable.
Whether the manual copy step is worth paying to remove.

candidates.reason: The fresh span documents a repeatable weekly workflow, but this is a product showcase rather than validated demand; no builder reference or buyer evidence supports a qualifying proposal.
